newsitem.title: UK: IPE states default rules in Nov gas oil standoff.
newsitem.headline: IPE states default rules in Nov gas oil standoff.

text.p: The International Petroleum Exchange (IPE) on Thursday reacted to charges by trader AIC that Cargill had defaulted on the November IPE gas oil contract by restating the regulations governing a situation in which one party fails to meet its obligations.

The London-based exchange said in a statement that in the event that it appeared to the clearing house that either party had defaulted, then the clearing house "would take such steps as it deems appropriate to acheive an amicable and equitable settlement."
If a settlement could not be reached then the clearing house would refer the issue to the directors of the IPE, the exchange said.

The statement added that if such a default included a failure by the seller to have product ready for delivery or failure by the buyer to accept delivery then the directors of the IPE would determine a price at which the contract would be invoiced back by the clearing house.
The IPE said this would be pursuant to rule K.13 of its regulations.

Trading house AIC, the main short on the contract, said earlier that Cargill, the dominant long, had failed to lift the required volume of gas oil in the first five-day period of the November 16-30 delivery window.
Cargill was due to take delivery of around 627,800 tonnes, of which a third each is due to be lifted in the three five-day periods, November 16-20, November 21-25 and November 26-30.
Cargill declined immediate comment on the AIC allegation. On Wednesday Cargill said it was working with the IPE to ensure orderly delivery in line with the spirit and letter of IPE regulations.

European gas oil traders have condemned a duel being fought between the two big trading houses on gas oil futures, saying it has killed liquidity, distorted supply patterns and blunted the IPE's price discovery function.
